common_name: French Red Shallot (Copper-Red Skinned True Shallot)

planting.note: Plant individual bulbs or sets in early spring (or fall in mild-winter zones) in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; French Red is a true shallot with coppery-red skin and rich, mild-pungent flavor.

directions: Plant individual bulbs pointed-end-up, just below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing 6-8 inches apart to allow each bulb to multiply into a cluster. French Red produces clusters of small, round-to-oval bulbs with distinctive coppery-red skin and pale purple-tinged flesh, carrying the rich, complex, mild-pungent flavor that distinguishes true shallots from ordinary onions and makes them prized in French cooking. Grow much like garlic, keeping soil evenly moist through bulb development and reducing water as the tops begin to yellow and fall over. Harvest when most of the foliage has died back, cure in a warm, dry, airy spot for two to three weeks, then store in a cool, dry location; shallots typically store longer than onions of similar size.

common_name: Camus de Bretagne Leek (Classic French Winter Leek)
scientific_name: Allium ampeloprasum var. porrum 'Camus de Bretagne'

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting, or start in summer for a fall and winter main crop; Camus de Bretagne is a classic French heirloom leek noted for exceptionally thick, short stalks and good cold tolerance.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting, or sow in summer for a main fall and winter crop, then set pencil-thick seedlings 4-6 inches apart into fertile, well-drained soil. Camus de Bretagne, a classic French heirloom leek from Brittany, is prized for exceptionally thick, short, sturdy stalks with a mild, sweet flavor and good cold tolerance that allows it to stand in the garden through cool weather without becoming tough. Hill or trench soil around the stems as they grow to blanch and lengthen the tender white portion. In the Gulf South's mild winters, it can often be left in the ground and harvested as needed through the cool season rather than lifted all at once, giving a long, flexible harvest window.
